title: DC-area forecast: Very humid tonight with another chance of late-day storms Friday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Just an isolated shower possible through the rest of the night. Otherwise very soupy with evening and overnight temperatures in the 70s.

What’s next? More days with highs near 90 or above are possible through the weekend as summer percolates. Late-day storm chances are also common.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Maybe an isolated shower this evening and overnight. Partly cloudy and still quite muggy with lows mainly in the low and mid-70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): Partly sunny with highs near 90 to the low 90s. Humidity remains high, with dew points around the low 70s making it feel as hot as the upper 90s to near 100. Decent chance of some scattered showers and storms moving in from the west after 3 p.m. or so, with the potential for a few to be strong. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Scattered showers and storms could continue to move west to east through the area until 8 or 9 p.m. Lows mainly dip into the low and mid-70s. Confidence: Medium-High

📬 Get our forecast in your inbox

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

More of the same through the weekend. Humidity may tail off just slightly with time, but dew points don‘t get much below 70, so it won't be too great. Both days seem to have late-day thunderstorm chances, perhaps higher Saturday than Sunday. Highs are near 90 or into the low 90s. Confidence: Medium-High

Still hot Monday and maybe into Tuesday as the next cold front approaches and eventually passes. We could punch into the low to mid-90s for highs before the front moves by. Additional shower and storm chances continue until it does. And even though there's a front, any relief could be short-lived. Confidence: Medium-High

DC weather history for August 6

Historic heat in 1918 pushed temperatures to 106 degrees—tying the all-time record—and marked one of the most extreme hot days ever observed in Washington.

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: We're getting late enough in the season I will gladly hate on high humidity with heat. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
